paper.title: Generalized Linear Bandits: Almost Optimal Regret with One-Pass Update

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized linear bandit (GLB) with time-varying arm sets and self-concordant link
unmapped: Link function is R-self-concordant: |mu''(z)| <= R mu'(z); the learner knows R
The learner knows the dispersion g(tau) of the canonical exponential family
Rewards may be unbounded (e.g. Poisson, Gaussian)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$, the learner selects an action $X_t \in \mathcal{X}_t \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ... conditioned on $\mathcal{F}_t$, the reward $r_t$ follows a canonical exponential family distribution with the natural parameter given by the linear model $z_t = X_t^\top\theta_*$. ... Assumption 1: $\norm{\x}_2 \leq 1$ ... $\norm{\theta_*}_2 \leq S$ for some constant $S > 0$ known to the learner. Assumption 2: $c_\mu \leq \mu'(z) \leq L_\mu$ for all $z \in [-S,S]$. Assumption 3: $|\mu''(z)| \leq R \mu'(z)$.

bound.expression_latex: dSR\sqrt{S^2R + \log T} \sqrt{\frac{T\log T}{\kappa_*}} + \kappa d^2S^2R^3 \log T (S^2R + \log T)

symbols.R_sc: self-concordance constant of the link, |mu''| <= R mu'
symbols.kappa_star: 1/((1/T) sum_t mu'(x_{t,*}^T theta_*)), inverse average slope at optimal actions
symbols.g_tau: dispersion g(tau) of the exponential family

tuning: lambda = max{14 d eta R^2, 6 eta R S L_mu / g(tau)}

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1]$. Under Assumptions 1, 2, and 3, with probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm 1 with parameter $\eta = 1 + RS$ and $\lambda = \max\{ 14d\eta R^2, 6\eta RS L_\mu/g(\tau) \}$ ensures $\Reg \lesssim dSR\sqrt{S^2R + \log T} \sqrt{\frac{T\log T}{\kappa_*}} + \kappa d^2S^2R^3 \log T (S^2R + \log T)$, where $\lesssim$ is used to hide constant independence of $d$, $\kappa$, $S$, $R$ and $T$.

results.notes: Regret is defined via mean rewards mu(x^T theta_*) against the per-round optimal action, and the bound holds with probability 1-delta. The paper writes argmin for x_{t,*}, but argmax is clearly intended. Per-round cost is O(d^3 + d^2|X_t|). The bound hides constants and polynomial dependence on L_mu and g(tau). Dependence on delta is hidden in the constant.
